Schema A machine-readable or documented definition of a data shape and its constraints. Idempotency A defined property where repeating an equivalent operation does not create additional unintended effects. Cursor pagination Pagination that continues from an opaque position in an ordered result set. Webhook An HTTP request sent by a provider to a registered consumer when an event occurs.

Recover with evidence instead of panic Repository A Git object database and references representing project history, usually with a working tree. Index The staging area containing the exact snapshot proposed for the next commit. Commit An immutable snapshot with metadata and parent link or links. Branch A movable reference that commonly points to the newest commit in a line of work. Remote A named connection to another Git repository and its tracked references. Pull request A GitHub collaboration proposal to review and integrate one branch into another.

Event A signal that something happened, such as input, navigation, or a network result. Progressive enhancement Delivering a functional baseline first and adding supported capabilities without making the baseline unusable.

title: The 7 Types of Databases
summary: Compare seven useful database families by the shape of their data, the questions they answer well, and the trade-offs they introduce.
sectionTitles: 1. Start with questions, not product names
2. Relational databases: connected facts with strong rules
3. Document databases: records shaped like application aggregates
4. Key–value databases: the shortest path to a known item
5. Graph databases: relationships are first-class data
6. Time-series, search, and vector databases
7. Use more than one database only for proven pressure
8. A practical selection matrix

Constraint A rule the database enforces to reject invalid data states. Index An additional data structure that speeds selected lookups at the cost of storage and write work. Transaction A unit of work whose changes are committed or rolled back according to defined guarantees. Projection A derived representation optimized for a particular read model, search, or analysis need.
